scenarios.name: Tool args must match user intent (party_size + time)
scenarios.description: User says 'book for 2 at 7pm'. The agent's natural-language reply may sound correct, but the actual `book_table(party_size, time)` arguments must match. An agent that calls `book_table(party_size=3, time="8pm")` will fail deterministically with `invalid_arguments` -- the failure message names the exact wrong fields. This is the kind of regression an LLM-as-judge text scorer typically misses.

turns.message: Please book a table for 2 people at 7pm tonight under the name Smith.

tools.name: book_table
tools.expected_response: Booking confirmed. Reference: B-7812. Party of 2 at 7pm, Smith.

turns.golden_response: Booked for 2 at 7pm under Smith. Confirmation: B-7812.

scenarios.expected_outcome: A booking exists for 2 people at 7pm under Smith, with a confirmation reference.
outcome_checks: Party size in the booking is 2 (not 3, not 4).
Time in the booking is 7pm (not 8pm or any other time).
